changelog.notes: Emulátoronként is áthozhatod a mentéseket, nem csak egyben: a Mentések fülön minden emulátor külön sorban áll a saját két dátumával, és külön hozható át. Így az is látszik, melyik boxon frissebb egy adott konzol mentése - egyetlen dátum a boxra ezt nem tudja megmondani, ha az egyik szobában SNES-szel, a másikban GameCube-bal játszottak. / You can bring saves per emulator now, not just all at once: the Saves tab lists each emulator on its own row with its own two dates and its own copy. That also shows which box has the fresher saves for a given console - one date per box cannot say, if one room played the SNES and the other the GameCube.

A Mentések fülön most már látod, melyik box mentése az újabb, mielőtt áthoznád: ott van a két dátum és hogy hány fájl frissebb a másik boxon. Ha valami ezen a boxon újabb, azt külön kiírja - a másolás azt is felülírná. / The Saves tab now shows which box has the newer saves before you bring anything over: both dates, and how many files are fresher on the other box. If something on this box is newer, it says so separately - a copy would replace that too.

Carry on in the other room: a new Saves tab brings your saves and save states over from another tvbox, so a game started on one TV can be finished on the other. It used to be a button in the box's own settings, which meant a TV with no emulator on it still talked about saves; the box now only asks whether the folders may be shared at all, and the rest is here. Connecting the two boxes is one code typed once - they can read each other from then on.

Your saves can travel to your other box. Turn it on in Settings > Network > Saves sharing, connect the two boxes once, and a game you started in one room can be carried to the other - save files and save states both. Nothing is ever sent back the other way, so two people playing in two rooms cannot overwrite each other: you go to the box you want the save on, and bring it there. What travels is the saves themselves - an emulator's own settings, its shader cache and its logs stay with the box they belong to.

Games can live anywhere the box can see: link a folder from a USB stick or a network share into the library. The app's own network-share setup is gone - the box mounts shares now (Settings > Network), and the app links a folder inside one. Uploading games from a phone moved into the app.

Games start again on a box running the new system software. RetroArch picks between two ways of drawing, and it decided by looking for a file the new version does not have - so it chose the one that cannot draw at all there, and a game came up black and closed itself.
Covers no longer flash up blank for a moment while you scroll the games grid.

Your game lists and in-game saves travel with the box's backup now. Which games are on which console, the saves a game writes for itself, and how you set the emulator up used to live only on that box: re-flash it, or set up a second one, and you started over. Three things stay out, because a backup goes through your phone and has to stay small: the game files themselves, the covers (the box fetches those again on its own), and save states - the snapshots you take from the emulator's own menu, which are far bigger than everything else put together.
Fixes the previous version: an emulator's own data files were looked up against the wrong list and so were never actually fetched.

Installing an emulator now brings the files it cannot run without. Some emulators need data of their own beside the program - PPSSPP wants its fonts and a flash image, ScummVM its engine data - and without them the emulator started and then said its system files were missing, naming none of them. libretro publishes those files, so the box fetches them with the emulator.

A console that arrived twice is one console again. Some games are catalogued under a separate database for their digital re-release - PSP titles bought from the store, for instance - and RetroArch made a second console out of them, named the same but with a bracket after it. It also looked like no emulator was installed for it, because no emulator advertises that name. The second one is now merged into the first as soon as a scan runs, and it plays with the emulator it always should have.

You can tell the box to read a folder for games now - the Scan tab. A console only appears under Games once a folder has been read for it, and nothing did that before: installing an emulator does not, and RetroArch's own scan silently skips every game it does not recognise from its database, which is most of a library made of bad dumps, hacks or homebrew. The box now runs that scan for the labels it gets right and then adds everything it left behind, so the games appear either way. It also says what it found in a folder before you press anything, and asks which console only when the file types genuinely cannot say. Covers follow a scan on their own, including for games whose file name carries a number in front of the title.

The games are on the box now. Opening RetroArch shows your own consoles and covers in a grid you can drive with the remote or a controller, and pressing OK starts the game straight away - no emulator menu in between, and when the game ends you are back in the list. Consoles and covers can be managed from the TV as well as from your phone. The Xbox/Guide button also opens the emulator's own menu mid-game (save states, close content) on pads where it previously did nothing: which button that is differs per controller, so the box now reads it from the controller itself instead of trusting one number.

Games have covers now. RetroArch only shows artwork for games in a scanned list and never fetches it, so the box does: it walks your lists and puts a cover in place for every game one exists for, by itself whenever the box is idle, and on demand from the new Artwork page on your phone. Its menu is also shorter - the dead core downloader, the disc entries this box has no drive for, and the pictures/music/videos tabs are gone, so the consoles come first.

OpenGL games work on the GPU now. Emulators that need OpenGL (OpenLara, Craft and most others) used to render on the processor, which made them unplayable; the box now picks the right graphics API per emulator from what that emulator itself declares, so the ones that need Vulkan keep using it.
The consoles page opens faster: the box no longer re-reads every installed emulator in full to check whether it is up to date.

Consoles are added from the box now: pick one and the emulator for it is downloaded and checked, with a note when a newer build appears. RetroArch's own Online Updater is hidden, because in this build it cannot fetch anything.
Consoles can be added again: RetroArch's core downloader had no address to fetch its list from, so it always answered "failed to retrieve core list".
Initial release: RetroArch on the TV, driven by the remote or a controller. Home always returns to the box.

description.en: Play retro games on the TV. The box shows your games as a grid of covers, grouped by console and driven with the remote; OK starts the game straight in the emulator, the Xbox/Guide button on a controller opens its menu mid-game, and Home always brings you back to the box. Consoles and covers are managed on the TV or from your phone; game files are uploaded from your phone, or read from a network share.
description.hu: Retro játékok a tévén. A box a saját borítós rácsában mutatja a játékokat konzolonként, távirányítóval kezelve; az OK egyenesen elindítja a játékot az emulátorban, kontrolleren az Xbox/Guide gomb játék közben előhozza az emulátor menüjét, a Home gomb pedig mindig visszahoz a boxra. A konzolokat és a borítókat a tévén vagy telefonról kezelheted; a játékfájlok telefonról töltődnek fel, vagy hálózati megosztásról olvassa őket.
